updates.assessment: Both sides now use real count/domain/service-aware write autocomplete, typed/ideal elevation, parent and sibling decorations, visible-height preference, keyboard highlight/selected/click entry, manual fetch, confirmed or skipped multiline paste. Paste only adds and removes the entered tag from the opposite side; each service preserves independent input drafts. Closing owner invalidates pending paste answers and stale Apply. Shared favourites/children tabs now use the configured count service for favourites decorators and descendant/display-count ordering for children; selected tags are excluded and applied limit/show-all feeds existing inputs. Shared right-click native menus now copy raw tags/subtags/underscores/counts/parents/all rows, toggle per-widget/per-tab decorations, manage favourites and per-service most-used with exact removal questions and reread concurrent writes, and launch raw child predicates through a weak main-window hook. Pending menus block owner editing/Apply and owner close invalidates questions/callbacks. Menus now query all real service display graphs for grouped siblings/ideal/parent/child entries and open owned relationship editors seeded on every service tab; owner close cancels child. Relationship dialogs consume configured default/remember preferences and preserve staged cancellation separately from immediate service memory. Per-widget file/tag-domain buttons now have checked menus and exact all-known interlocks, preserve independent service drafts, feed real query/count/decorator/children consumers and use an owned staged multiple/deleted selector; cancelling does not write options or damage input domains. Shared logical multi-selection; plain/Ctrl/reversible Shift and Ctrl+Shift; inherited parent-row origin; unchanged fetch/decorations retain batch; Enter/double-click activates batch in ManageTags, both relationship sides and detached child. Cancel/reopen and stale callbacks retain staged owner boundaries. No new completed original-ID count. All recorded multi-tag local context paths: selected tags/subtags/underscores/counts/deduplicated parents clipboard copies, AND/OR/each-tag/duplicate native page launches, whole-selection relationship child seeds. Selected-tag maintenance records exact warning/title/buttons and repairs connected storage/display counts and subtag indexes across services/domains; preserves mappings/relations and unrelated caches; Cancel/stale owners discard pending answers. No new completed original-ID count. Accepted clipboard additions preserve caller text drafts and result selection. Declining the multiline question resumes native paste at retained cursor/selection, preserving raw newlines exactly; undo/redo restore recorded drafts. A small TextInput wrapper disables single-line only during paste, retaining native editor engine. Both relationship inputs, ManageTags and detached editors consume it; closed owners ignore pending answers. Real result-keyboard sequence: logical arrow wrapping; reversible Shift/Ctrl+Shift selection; Home/End endpoints; physical-row PageUp/PageDown including expanded parent rows; CtrlP/N; focused result CtrlA; ordered CtrlC and deduplicated parents on CtrlShiftC. Native selected editor text keeps its own copy engine. All three owner callbacks guard pending operations and closed owners; navigation keeps draft unchanged and scrolls to last hit. Focused Escape clears selected results without entering tags/changing draft/cancelling owner; second Escape propagates cancellation. All three native owner key-capture layers delegate after their popup/pending guards. A persistent non-repeated pointer surface records and consumes real press/move/release: range addition/reversal, inherited parent origin, Ctrl deselection start and reversible removal/restoration. Pointer handlers survive replaced suggestions models. Each input owns replacement history: paste is atomic; caret movement, intervening Undo/Redo and changed deletion direction split commands, while adjacent typing/same-direction deletion coalesces. Fresh edits invalidate redo; Unicode selection replay converts recorded Qt UTF16 units to native UTF8 byte offsets. Recorded replacement selection/owner isolation remains separate from the broader shared input.

updates.assessment: Actual Qt seconds/milliseconds fields default to 600 ms, clamp minimum 20 ms, and have 59/999 field maxima. Cancel retains raw imported milliseconds; unchanged Apply accepts displayed fields once without overwriting a concurrent policy, and explicit edits preserve their actual float-sum conversion (1 s 29 ms saves 1029 ms and reopens at 1 s 28 ms). Native-wins retained ClientOptions load, future import, field-scoped save and hidden/retired controls reach the real maintenance consumer. Each pass snapshots its saved delay; each admitted file/thumbnail pair commits its durable queue clear then waits outside the writer, including the final pair and a missing original. Successors recheck current queue/membership/shared-media/import claims. Restored local media only clears an inconsistent queue and does not perform or wait for a physical pair; actual reference re-add clears those queues before the loop. Owned worker shutdown wakes bounded waits, retires further admissions and joins on normal shutdown. Failed pairs remain queued and receive no successful-pair wait; earlier pairs stay committed. Broader maintenance parents remain Partial.

All six Options labels, defaults, imported settings, Cancel/save/reopen and invalid-index behavior are directly replayed at model/Store level. The real GUI Options replay toggles the wheel checkbox; the drag consumer regression sets saved preferences through its test setup rather than separately driving the other three Options checkbox controls.

The actual Qt recording uses synthetic QDropEvent source() to supply the source TabBar and instruments QDrag.exec_ to record offers/return IgnoreAction. The native Qt OS drag loop, cancellation/drop routing and cross-window behavior are not recorded.

The native persistent in-window TouchArea supports page-tab reorder/nested transfer. OS QDrag pixmap/cursor, cross-window/tree drag, media/file/external drops and empty-notebook content-body drop remain outside this scope.

No Qt PNG is authored by record_tab_drag.py. updates.label: When there are too many tabs to fit, '...' elide their names so they fit:
updates.assessment: The page tab names checkbox stages/persists/imports/reopens with default true. The actual native tab label uses measured glyph widths and per-input fitting state to paint a middle ellipsis only when overflow requires it; the stored/decorated label and full tooltip remain unchanged. The overflow probe uses the same selected600/unselected400 glyph weights as the painted tab, so a near-fit selected name triggers fitting rather than mistakenly scrolling.

updates.label: Always Loop Animations:
updates.assessment: Exact Always Loop Animations checkbox defaulttrue stages until Apply, persists and imports always_loop_gifs. Native animation players in media viewer/archive-delete/duplicate filters read the preference at each wrap and honor file play counts when false, pausing on the final frame after the stored count. Stored0 and ugoira mean infinite; missing GIF loop metadata means1. The existing mpv consumer captures GIF/APNG metadata at file load, pauses/seeks to start after the finite restart count and uses newly applied preference on the next load. Slideshow stop remains independent. Fresh actual Qt decoding/painting/timer output covers stored0/1/2 with forced looping on/off; separate real GIF/APNG reads cover finite/infinite/absent metadata. Tests cover controls, migration, decoded-native finite pause/live changes, owned viewer final-frame stability/resume, Cancel/reopen and existing MPV backend when available.
limitations: This adds no absent animation backend. Native animation decoding remains WebP/ugoira; existing GIF/APNG playback requires libmpv. The MPV regression runs only where libmpv is available, as existing player tests do; metadata parsing and native decoded-frame regressions are unconditional. Existing MPV restart polling behavior is retained. Enabling looping does not resume already paused media, matching the reference.
remaining_limitations: This adds no absent animation backend. Native animation decoding remains WebP/ugoira; existing GIF/APNG playback requires libmpv. The MPV regression runs only where libmpv is available, as existing player tests do; metadata parsing and native decoded-frame regressions are unconditional. The note editor uses an owned native multiline TextInput and inline naming/cancel questions. Its cursor/anchor use UTF-8 bytes while Qt uses UTF-16 positions; regression translates offsets and compares actual Unicode keyboard insertion. Cog entries/separator are source-declared real Slint MenuItems; no unsupported materialized OS-menu introspection claimed.

Native Options writes only changed fields and retains unedited concurrent preferences, while cog changes use an atomic read/edit/write of the latest typed setting. Retired owner and unanswered child guards, frozen file target, reopen/import and no file-note changes on Cancel are authored native boundaries. No reference parity is claimed for programmatic concurrent dialogs beyond the recorded reachable workflows.

Qt PNG captures closed-cog Manage Notes panel, no open cog menu, Notes Options checkbox pane or viewer-hover screenshot. Behavioral recording covers those actions; no matching Qt PNG for native hover.

Broader Manage Notes, viewer interaction and Notes Options parents remain Partial. Left-click note editing/right-click hide, keyboard Apply and empty-tab double-click are outside scope.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete image-cache controls are in scope for these assessments. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, image-tile, video buffers and global backend parity remain Partial with zero extra credit; no aliases or structural completions. The separate prefetch-per-viewer percentage is reviewed independently and receives no credit from these three image-cache assessments.

Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Inline native duration fields preserve untouched raw299 seconds and enforce the actual300-second edit minimum; the Qt duration-popup geometry is a separate presentation difference. Monitor screen estimates use the owning physical monitor converted to logical size; headless windows without a monitor omit that caption rather than invent screen dimensions.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.
The primary image shows saved cache=100B, timeout=5 minutes and storage=50%; its default previous=2, next=3, percentage=25% and pairs=3 are distinct from the saved prefetch producer.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete image-cache controls are in scope for these assessments. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, image-tile, video buffers and global backend parity remain Partial with zero extra credit; no aliases or structural completions. The separate prefetch-per-viewer percentage is reviewed independently and receives no credit from these three image-cache assessments.

Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Inline native duration fields preserve untouched raw299 seconds and enforce the actual300-second edit minimum; the Qt duration-popup geometry is a separate presentation difference. Monitor screen estimates use the owning physical monitor converted to logical size; headless windows without a monitor omit that caption rather than invent screen dimensions.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.
The primary image shows saved cache=100B, timeout=5 minutes and storage=50%; its default previous=2, next=3, percentage=25% and pairs=3 are distinct from the saved prefetch producer.

publication_policy.reason: The owner uses Linux and prioritizes validated Linux delivery. macOS is low priority; Windows is deferred because its builds materially lengthen validation. Secondary-platform CI remains available by explicit opt-in.

Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, image-tile, video buffers and global backend parity remain Partial with zero extra credit; no aliases or structural completions. Qt uses a controller-global ImageRendererCache. Native owns one cache per Main binding incarnation, shared by its real preview, still viewer, archive/delete and duplicate filter; standalone duplicate filters own separate policy-bound caches. Final Bound-clone drop, rebind and accepted close permanently retire admission while retained worker/callback handles cannot revive it.

Full still-image cache bytes are pending metadata RGB estimates and loaded RGB/RGBA raster bytes recounted at access. The cache admits one incoming item above its soft bound until maintenance, matching Qt. Pending decoders, accepted per-page 64MiB preview snapshots, current canvas/source/resize buffers, Slint image copies, playback and total process/GPU memory are separate presentation/resource ownership and are not evicted or counted as cache bytes.

Percentage uses strict estimated-size admission and applies only to future misses; existing admitted renderers remain subject to ordinary byte/idle maintenance. Saved policy and ICC changes refresh without resetting current accepted media, zoom, generation/page identity or viewing intervals. Future duplicate copies can only reuse cache-owned full rasters, while the current presentation remains independently retained.

Failed full-image and non-image thumbnail/poster fallback remain uncached; decoder injection keeps the public preview Decoder contract and bypasses the production cache. Existing worker bounds and late-publication generation guards are retained. Imported partial resolution falls back to100x100 exactly; real media metadata/ICC identity displaces stale cached sources.

Inline native duration fields preserve untouched raw299 seconds and enforce the actual300-second edit minimum; the Qt duration-popup geometry is a separate presentation difference. Monitor screen estimates use the owning physical monitor converted to logical size; headless windows without a monitor omit that caption rather than invent screen dimensions.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete prefetch controls are in scope. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.

The represented GeneralImage full-resolution raster path admits only the effective supported native static-image display action. Qt global renderer/controller ownership, image-project/unsupported codecs, tile/GPU/video renderer prefetch remain broader Partial boundaries.

One lazily started worker per viewer owner admits at most one real miss per readiness pass and coalesces one latest pending navigation. Saved policy and ICC/candidate-action changes capture a new navigation generation. Cache finished-image notifications resume the same captured generation, including another owner’s completion, without publishing SetMedia or viewing intervals. Idle/pending waits hold no Store; in-flight existing disk IO retains its Store until completion and is never joined on the UI.

Current native rendering reuses ready shared Arc rasters but performs its pre-existing synchronous decode independently while warm work is pending. Duplicate overlap decode remains a broader renderer architecture difference from Qt shared asynchronous current-renderer objects; it does not evade the warm budget or count presentation references as cache bytes.

Current image prefix and circular wrap duplicates count their ready actual bytes exactly as Qt. Unknown-resolution misses abort; refusal blocks later small candidates. Total/single prefetch thresholds allow equality, cache admission remains strict, and an uncached successful equality decode repeats on readiness. Atomic easy-space flushing scans only finished entries and deletes none when strict free-space > incoming estimate cannot be reached.

Hidden viewers may continue admitted warm work, as real Qt Canvas does. Close/replacement/rebind/accepted Main close and final Bound-clone drop retire admission; retained GUI/cache handles cannot revive it. Current pixels/zoom/viewing intervals and accepted preview-page snapshots remain independently owned.

Decode failures retain existing native blank/fallback behavior rather than creating Qt error-placeholder renderers. Public preview Decoder injection, two-worker publication bounds, late page/generation guards and ICC identity remain unchanged. Duplicate count is imported/defaulted for this percentage consumer only; no duplicate-count Options row or leaf credit is added.
No physical-display or wider platform parity is inferred from headless Linux native execution; Windows/macOS validation remains deferred under the exact-source owner policy.
Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.

The primary image shows saved previous=1, next=1 and percentage=50%, with cache=400B. The eight helper captures intentionally show default previous=2, next=3 and percentage=25%; they supplement geometry rather than replace saved-state proof. Both actual producers retain default duplicate_pairs=3 and supply no pair-count credit.

publication_policy.reason: The owner uses Linux and prioritizes validated Linux delivery. macOS is low priority; Windows is deferred because its builds materially lengthen validation. Secondary-platform CI remains available by explicit opt-in.

limitations: Only the three frozen original concrete prefetch controls are in scope. Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.

The represented GeneralImage full-resolution raster path admits only the effective supported native static-image display action. Qt global renderer/controller ownership, image-project/unsupported codecs, tile/GPU/video renderer prefetch remain broader Partial boundaries.

One lazily started worker per viewer owner admits at most one real miss per readiness pass and coalesces one latest pending navigation. Saved policy and ICC/candidate-action changes capture a new navigation generation. Cache finished-image notifications resume the same captured generation, including another owner’s completion, without publishing SetMedia or viewing intervals. Idle/pending waits hold no Store; in-flight existing disk IO retains its Store until completion and is never joined on the UI.

Current native rendering reuses ready shared Arc rasters but performs its pre-existing synchronous decode independently while warm work is pending. Duplicate overlap decode remains a broader renderer architecture difference from Qt shared asynchronous current-renderer objects; it does not evade the warm budget or count presentation references as cache bytes.

Current image prefix and circular wrap duplicates count their ready actual bytes exactly as Qt. Unknown-resolution misses abort; refusal blocks later small candidates. Total/single prefetch thresholds allow equality, cache admission remains strict, and an uncached successful equality decode repeats on readiness. Atomic easy-space flushing scans only finished entries and deletes none when strict free-space > incoming estimate cannot be reached.

Hidden viewers may continue admitted warm work, as real Qt Canvas does. Close/replacement/rebind/accepted Main close and final Bound-clone drop retire admission; retained GUI/cache handles cannot revive it. Current pixels/zoom/viewing intervals and accepted preview-page snapshots remain independently owned.

Decode failures retain existing native blank/fallback behavior rather than creating Qt error-placeholder renderers. Public preview Decoder injection, two-worker publication bounds, late page/generation guards and ICC identity remain unchanged. Duplicate count is imported/defaulted for this percentage consumer only; no duplicate-count Options row or leaf credit is added.
No physical-display or wider platform parity is inferred from headless Linux native execution; Windows/macOS validation remains deferred under the exact-source owner policy.
Image-cache/image-prefetch/Speed-and-Memory structural parents, prefetch/shared renderer backend families, tile/video/cache-delay and the separate duplicate-pair-count control receive zero credit.
Validation is Linux only at this exact source and run; Windows and macOS are explicitly deferred, not passed.

The Qt PNGs have different staged values, accordion states and framework/font geometry from the final native states. This review confirms scoped readable controls, ordering and reference behavior; it does not claim pixel parity.

Exactly the six selected concrete controls receive review credit. Structural parents, general renderer/backend/tile/video/playback families and the separate duplicate-pair-count control retain broader Partial scope and zero extra credit.

All ten fresh native captures and both Qt PNGs were actually inspected. The unchanged strict finite/positive/bounds/positive-gap/long-warning geometry assertions passed. At 900px, long labels and the warning wrap readably; lower unselected controls remain scrollable rather than all-visible evidence.

The primary image shows saved previous=1, next=1 and percentage=50%, with cache=400B. The eight helper captures intentionally show default previous=2, next=3 and percentage=25%; they supplement geometry rather than replace saved-state proof. Both actual producers retain default duplicate_pairs=3 and supply no pair-count credit.

reference_source.symbol: EXPERIMENTAL: Minimum gallery importer update time:

updates.assessment: Exact independent staged gallery seconds/milliseconds minimum with a 250 ms lower bound and 59 s/999 ms constructor fields; reference defaults 1000 ms/30, typed raw legacy import, cancelled/retained Apply rejection, unchanged constructor-bound acceptance, field-scoped concurrent merge and save/reopen. Saved values reach the real visible current-page gallery list/totals scheduler: every 250 ms GUI tick checks strict now>pending deadline, samples displayed row count before refresh, sets next=now+max(minimum_ms/1000,rows/denominator), uses 1 s zero-denominator fallback, and force refresh resets the deadline to 0. Saved changes preserve the pending deadline and affect the next period. Highlighted jobs/tab progress/close eligibility stay live separately. Same-binding tab roundtrips retain offscreen/pre-deadline snapshots and refresh overdue returns. Hidden owners skip reads; rebind and accepted close permanently reject old retained refresh/sync, including close/re-show; cancelled close stays live.

updates.label: EXPERIMENTAL: Minimum watcher importer update time:

reference_source.symbol: EXPERIMENTAL: Minimum watcher importer update time:

updates.assessment: Exact independent staged watcher seconds/milliseconds minimum with a 250 ms lower bound and 59 s/999 ms constructor fields; reference defaults 1000 ms/30, typed raw legacy import, cancelled/retained Apply rejection, unchanged constructor-bound acceptance, field-scoped concurrent merge and save/reopen. Saved values reach the real visible current-page watcher list/totals scheduler: every 250 ms GUI tick checks strict now>pending deadline, samples displayed row count before refresh, sets next=now+max(minimum_ms/1000,rows/denominator), uses 1 s zero-denominator fallback, and force refresh resets the deadline to 0. Saved changes preserve the pending deadline and affect the next period. Highlighted jobs/tab progress/close eligibility stay live separately. Same-binding tab roundtrips retain offscreen/pre-deadline snapshots and refresh overdue returns. Hidden owners skip reads; rebind and accepted close permanently reject old retained refresh/sync, including close/re-show; cancelled close stays live.

updates.label: Use blurhash missing thumbnail fallback:
updates.assessment: Default-on typed checkbox and native-wins retained ClientOptions upgrade preserve saved false values. Cancel, Apply, reopen and field-scoped concurrent merge reach the actual owned thumbnail loader. Admitted requests copy geometry and recovery policy; failed stored-thumbnail/regeneration loads decode retained FileInfo.blurhash using the actual reference component/gamma/base83 rules, 32x32 recovery wrapper and reference resizing. Invalid/absent/disabled values publish the bundled default without physical regeneration or metadata writes. Saved toggle invalidates the cache and rejects held old generations before pending/cache mutation; real missing-original/thumbnail native replay keeps valid source metadata before false Apply and asserts different default pixels. Stored encoded-thumbnail ICC independence is preserved.

updates.label: Search predicate undo history

native_source.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

updates.assessment: Frame-owned, transient, separate deduplicated addition/removal recency lists populate the actual searching submenus newest first. Typed stable commands toggle the selected historical predicate on the currently visible media page, retire its entry before recording the resulting delta, and leave stale commands inert. New/restored page predicates do not enter history; histories survive page close/restore, apply across pages and stay independent across windows. Committed typed OR is one entry; cancelled predicate children and refused inputs add none. Undo enters a locked page hidden query while retaining its lock; with an empty notebook selected, it preserves history. Clear history uses the exact reference confirmation: rejection retains both lists; acceptance clears both without changing searches or closed-page history. History names use raw predicate text despite hidden-namespace presentation. Populated locked pages retain their prior lock badge and media even with synchronization enabled; locking and hash synchronization update the cached panel count. Accepted system values preserve originating Shift intent: drafts extend without frame history; normal activation merges into one committed OR history entry. Accepting a system value and later cancelling its outer OR leaves frame history unchanged while retaining actual reference recent predicates.

evidence.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

limitations: Native menu entries do not yet expose the reference status-bar tooltips explaining that results depend on the visible query.

Within one multi-predicate delta, native recency follows deterministic predicate order; reference Python set-difference ordering can vary across processes. Single-entry and cross-event recency, recorded batch outputs, and canonical identities are covered by authored replay.

updates.label: close and reload current gui session
updates.assessment: Exact Help/debug/gui action freezes the current ordered tree, files and importer options/logs, asynchronously commits/loads a private immutable Store snapshot, removes its slot, then forcibly closes the current pages without a question and reconstructs fresh page and importer identities. Actual Qt first-root/first-child selection and empty-thumbnail-selection reset are retained. Closed original pages remain undoable with original queues paused; restored queues start fresh and retain captured settings/logs. Later edits/new pages cannot alter the admitted snapshot. Hidden new requests are refused but admitted work delivers while Main is hidden. Weak Main/Pages and weak timer callbacks, permanent binding retirement and shared final-Bound-clone lease reject late completions after accepted exit/rebind/final-clone/Main destruction; Exit Cancel preserves admitted work.

limitations: Native unique private snapshot rows are not exposed as saved session names; Qt uses a fixed temporary named session. Overlapping native captures therefore cannot overwrite one another.
The existing synchronous snapshot-capture and final restore/close Store boundaries remain on the UI thread; broader large-session responsiveness is outside this debug action.
Already-running Store work finishes and removes its slot after retirement; its reply cannot replace pages. Native IO diagnostics use the existing main-window note instead of the Qt exception popup.
Manual save-last-session, wider session/debug GUI/style families and parent/alias nodes receive no credit.

The real native earliest-deadline weak single-shot timer rechecks the monotonic clock and polls owner/dismissal liveness at most 200ms; event-loop delivery can occur later. The actual 250ms popup projection timer is exercised only for Show resumption after durable hidden publication.

Hidden Main refuses new admission while already-admitted deadlines publish to Store; hidden cards remain frozen until Show refresh. Durable native Store jobs/reopen are explicit native behavior, not a claim that Qt persists its transient JobStatus cards.

The weak-window and Owner-drop regressions prove producer retirement without retaining Main. Retained Control handles still own their State and Store until those handles are dropped; this packet does not claim immediate release of every Store owner on GUI retirement.

Reference ThumbnailCache is process-wide. Native cache is owned by one main GUI incarnation and shared across its pages; separate main windows do not share raster entries. Apply updates the currently owned cache immediately. Rebind and accepted exit retire rows and cancel their staged Options owner, while declined exit preserves both.

Native cache accounts decoded RGB/RGBA buffer bytes and 128 bytes for a missing-thumbnail entry. Reference HydrusBitmap may store compressed data. Renderer-held image clones, loader queues, metadata/icon caches and total process/GPU memory are outside this finite accounted budget. As in reference, admission may overflow by one incoming entry until maintenance; this is not a hard total-memory ceiling.

Timeout uses monotonic last access and strict older-than expiry. Existing 25ms owned main collection ticks perform maintenance without requiring a new thumbnail request. Native inline day/hour/minute editing preserves untouched raw 299 seconds and enforces 300 seconds once edited; the reference duration-popup geometry remains outside this slice.

No recorded Qt PNG shows the clear-action menu or post-clear state. The source-grounded reference QAction recording proves clear_thumbnail_cache plus notify_complete_thumbnail_reset and empty cache keys; fresh native menu/reload stills plus unchanged reset/generation/owner regressions support this action, without pixel parity. Historical Qt cache Options at 1 day and native saved 5 minutes are different fixture states.

The visible nearby clear-all-rendering-caches entry receives no credit from this action. The native key callback route is exercised with real rendered menu placement; this evidence does not claim every OS input or all Help/debug menu behavior.

Nonfinal Bound clones, temporary Main hide and pending/declined exit preserve drafts. Retained warning adapters/windows are tested; the private SessionDialog component is not separately exposed.

Native dedicated editor/notice captures preserve the finite controls/messages but differ from Qt in font metrics, spacing, input height/width, star/icon styling, large vertical notice OK and outer Apply footer topology. No whole-dialog pixel/geometry equality, OS chrome/modality/focus, clipboard bitmap equality or arbitrary shared-editor ownership is claimed.
Validation is Linux only; Windows and macOS are deferred. No parent, alias, generic active-edit, global-radio or additional-family completion credit.

Typed FileHashes use deterministic set ordering where Qt explicit tuples may retain ordering; algorithm/sign/query membership and raw cleanup first-valid-occurrence order remain. Forced cleanup exact You sure? is inline and freezes the draft; owned native warning lacks Qt icon.

The550x330 invalid-acceptance warning is separate evidence. The700x560 actual bad-lines-normal cleanup notice is the four-section Qt warning comparison; larger native geometry/button and icon differences remain.
remaining_limitations: Existing forced cleanup exact You sure? yes/no question remains inline in its owner and freezes the draft; warning notices are separate owned windows. Native notice styling uses the existing Slint notice rather than Qt warning icon.

Native typed FileHashes are deterministic sets: explicit reconstruction sorts hash lines where Qt can retain tuple order. Algorithm, sign and query membership are preserved; raw cleanup preserves first valid occurrence order.

Generic active-predicate Edit remains a separate scope. Explicit supplied-input reconstruction is model-covered; native reopen uses the real saved typed custom default. Global Enter-on-radio preference remains excluded; the recorded true-default Enter path is supported.
No hash family, sign sibling, Options/predicate parent or shared/structural editor alias is promoted. Other predicate kinds retain their widgets and parser/query behavior.

Qt destruction recording covers two nonmodal standalone QWidget.window() parent cascades with retained wrappers and unchanged blank predicates. It does not destroy client Main, run nested exec() teardown or establish active nested-warning closure. Native notice closure is a separate safety boundary.

Native Main-death cleanup is observed through a repeated 50 ms timer with a bounded test deadline; final Bound-owner drop closes synchronously. Strong headless warning adapters/windows are retained in native notice tests; the private SessionDialog component is not separately exposed. OS chrome, modality, focus or destruction geometry equality is not claimed.

publication_policy.reason: The owner uses Linux and prioritizes validated Linux delivery. macOS is low priority; Windows is deferred because its builds materially lengthen validation. Secondary-platform CI remains available by explicit opt-in.

Pending menus block owner editing/Apply and owner close invalidates questions/callbacks. Menus now query all real service display graphs for grouped siblings/ideal/parent/child entries and open owned relationship editors seeded on every service tab; owner close cancels child. Relationship dialogs consume configured default/remember preferences and preserve staged cancellation separately from immediate service memory. Per-widget file/tag-domain buttons now have checked menus and exact all-known interlocks, preserve independent service drafts, feed real query/count/decorator/children consumers and use an owned staged multiple/deleted selector; cancelling does not write options or damage input domains. Shared logical multi-selection; plain/Ctrl/reversible Shift and Ctrl+Shift; inherited parent-row origin; unchanged fetch/decorations retain batch; Enter/double-click activates batch in ManageTags, both relationship sides and detached child. Cancel/reopen and stale callbacks retain staged owner boundaries. No new completed original-ID count. All recorded multi-tag local context paths: selected tags/subtags/underscores/counts/deduplicated parents clipboard copies, AND/OR/each-tag/duplicate native page launches, whole-selection relationship child seeds. Selected-tag maintenance records exact warning/title/buttons and repairs connected storage/display counts and subtag indexes across services/domains; preserves mappings/relations and unrelated caches; Cancel/stale owners discard pending answers. No new completed original-ID count. Accepted clipboard additions preserve caller text drafts and result selection. Declining the multiline question resumes native paste at retained cursor/selection, preserving raw newlines exactly; undo/redo restore recorded drafts. A small TextInput wrapper disables single-line only during paste, retaining native editor engine. Both relationship inputs, ManageTags and detached editors consume it; closed owners ignore pending answers. Real result-keyboard sequence: logical arrow wrapping; reversible Shift/Ctrl+Shift selection; Home/End endpoints; physical-row PageUp/PageDown including expanded parent rows; CtrlP/N; focused result CtrlA; ordered CtrlC and deduplicated parents on CtrlShiftC. Native selected editor text keeps its own copy engine. All three owner callbacks guard pending operations and closed owners; navigation keeps draft unchanged and scrolls to last hit. Focused Escape clears selected results without entering tags/changing draft/cancelling owner; second Escape propagates cancellation. All three native owner key-capture layers delegate after their popup/pending guards. A persistent non-repeated pointer surface records and consumes real press/move/release: range addition/reversal, inherited parent origin, Ctrl deselection start and reversible removal/restoration. Pointer handlers survive replaced suggestions models. Each input owns replacement history: paste is atomic; caret movement, intervening Undo/Redo and changed deletion direction split commands, while adjacent typing/same-direction deletion coalesces. Fresh edits invalidate redo; Unicode selection replay converts recorded Qt UTF16 units to native UTF8 byte offsets. Recorded replacement selection/owner isolation remains separate from the broader shared input.

updates.label: Search predicate undo history

native_source.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

updates.assessment: Frame-owned, transient, separate deduplicated addition/removal recency lists populate the actual searching submenus newest first. Typed stable commands toggle the selected historical predicate on the currently visible media page, retire its entry before recording the resulting delta, and leave stale commands inert. New/restored page predicates do not enter history; histories survive page close/restore, apply across pages and stay independent across windows. Committed typed OR is one entry; cancelled predicate children and refused inputs add none. Undo enters a locked page hidden query while retaining its lock; with an empty notebook selected, it preserves history. Clear history uses the exact reference confirmation: rejection retains both lists; acceptance clears both without changing searches or closed-page history. History names use raw predicate text despite hidden-namespace presentation. Populated locked pages retain their prior lock badge and media even with synchronization enabled; locking and hash synchronization update the cached panel count. Accepted system values preserve originating Shift intent: drafts extend without frame history; normal activation merges into one committed OR history entry. Accepting a system value and later cancelling its outer OR leaves frame history unchanged while retaining actual reference recent predicates.

evidence.description: Inspected this native subsystem and its callbacks; Reference keeps added/removed predicate batches and builds addition/removal submenus; native SearchPage enters/removes predicates without a matching undo-history model.

remaining_limitations: Native menu entries do not yet expose the reference status-bar tooltips explaining that results depend on the visible query.

Within one multi-predicate delta, native recency follows deterministic predicate order; reference Python set-difference ordering can vary across processes. Single-entry and cross-event recency, recorded batch outputs, and canonical identities are covered by authored replay.
Rust model/native compilation, regression execution and native rendering await hosted CI. No full completion promotion is proposed.
